title: Exposure-and-sharpness nuisance randomisation: every training view is re-photographed at random (brightness, contrast, gamma, colour balance, saturation, blur, sensor noise) so a pixel fingerprint of one survey stops being a usable solution
hypothesis: The three-survey training signal of experiment 2 did not teach exposure invariance; it taught three exposures. Design-stage probe on experiment 2's exported berlin.onnx, scored with the frozen scorer's own 400 eval crops (numbers from the design stage, not part of the record): on its OWN training photograph truedop_2023 the model reads 0.087, but the same photograph +20 on every pixel reads 1.240 (usable 94.3% -> 14.7%), -20 reads 1.550, and a 1 px Gaussian blur reads 1.100 (median 29 m -> 253 m). That is the identical brittleness the era's founding table measured on the single-photograph champion (+20 -> 1.453, blur -> 1.271): three photographs with three different colour balances (channel means 118/121/117, 99/98/99, 117/116/110) were absorbed as three pixel-exact fingerprints, not as an invariance, and nothing in the training signal asks for one. Globally matching the held-out 2024 photograph's per-channel mean/std to truedop_2023 recovers only a fifth of the gap (1.583 -> 1.365, false fix 65% -> 47%, usable 7% -> 10%), so the rest of the gap is LOCAL: the 2024 survey is softer and lower-contrast (channel std 41/39/40 vs 50/47/43) with its own shadows, resampling and 1 m texture, and the model's fix rides exactly that 1 m texture (hence the blur result). Experiment 3 tried to forbid fingerprints at the feature level and was reverted, but its mechanism never bit: the logged cross-survey cosine was already 0.966 at epoch 1 on a freshly initialised network, because post-ReLU GAP features are non-negative and share a large common component, so a cosine floor of 0.9 was satisfied for free and the term's gradient was negligible (cons 0.065 against a cross-entropy of 2.9). Its refutation is of a vacuous constraint, not of feature invariance; a fair retest needs batch-centred features. The direct remedy for what the probe measured is the library's L2 entry #2: randomise, per training view, the nuisances that differ between exposures of the same ground (global intensity, contrast, gamma, per-channel colour balance, saturation, sharpness, sensor noise). A pixel-exact fingerprint then no longer predicts the cell across the model's own training stream, so capacity has to move to what survives those transformations, which is the layout structure at 2 m scale and up that all four surveys share. The blur component is the load-bearing one for the cross-survey question: it is the 1 m texture that is survey-specific, and the exp-2 model demonstrably depends on it. This cannot synthesise leaf-off versus canopy or a different shadow direction; the three surveys supply that part, and this experiment makes them the only route left.
method: ONE change, in model/train.py only: a training-time augmentation stage augment_views(xb) applied on the GPU to every mini-batch right after xb is formed (float [B,3,128,128] in [0,1]), with independent random parameters per view: separable Gaussian blur sigma~U(0,1.5) px applied with probability 0.7 (7-tap, per-sample kernel via grouped conv); exposure gain~U(0.75,1.30) times per-channel colour gain~U(0.85,1.15); contrast~U(0.6,1.4) about the crop's own mean; brightness offset~U(-0.12,0.12); gamma~U(0.7,1.4); saturation~U(0.5,1.5) toward the per-pixel grey; additive Gaussian sensor noise sigma~U(0,0.03); clamp to [0,1]. Targets, loss, paired-position batching, model, decode, export, schedule and views per epoch are untouched; the exported graph is byte-for-byte the same architecture. train_info.json records the augmentation ranges.
expected_outcome: Mechanical check that must hold or the augmentation was not applied: re-running the design-stage probe on the new berlin.onnx (truedop_2023 eval crops +20 / -20 / 1 px blur) must read below 0.3 on all three, down from 1.24 / 1.55 / 1.10 on experiment 2's model; and the gap between 2024 raw and 2024 globally colour-matched (0.22 on experiment 2) should close to within 0.05. Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.583 -> predicted 1.15-1.40, from the false-fix rate falling (65% -> 35-50%) as confidence stops keying on one survey's intensities and sharpness, and usable rising (7% -> 15-30%) where the shared 2 m-scale structure is enough to name the 128 m cell. Training diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023: 0.060 / 0.053 / 0.088) are expected to worsen mildly to 0.08-0.25 because the pixel-exact route is closed; that is acceptable and is the sign capacity moved. Train top1 will read lower than experiment 2's 0.79 because it is now measured on augmented views; judge by eval. Decision rules: (a) 2024 improves AND the mechanical checks pass -> supported; the next experiment attacks the remaining local gap with something the augmentation cannot synthesise: either experiment 3's feature consistency re-done on batch-centred features (its cosine was vacuous), or aligned cross-survey patch mixing (compose one training view from pixel-aligned patches of two surveys), or L2 #3 distillation. (b) mechanical checks pass but 2024 stays >= 1.5 -> exposure/sharpness is not what separates a fourth survey; the gap is season and shadow geometry, and the next move is cross-survey structure (consistency with centred features, or distillation), not more augmentation. (c) mechanical checks fail -> the ranges were too narrow or the stage was skipped; fix before concluding anything. Standing check: the score must improve through usable_fix_rate and a lower false-fix rate, with coverage on 2024 staying >= 0.2 (currently 0.72).
eli5: The model had three photographs of Berlin and learned each one by its exact brightness, colour tint and fine grain, like recognising a page by the paper it is printed on rather than by the words. A test showed it: brighten its own training photo slightly and it is lost. Now every training picture is handed to it slightly re-photographed at random each time, a bit brighter or darker, warmer or cooler, softer or sharper, grainier, so the paper keeps changing and only the words, the streets and building outlines, stay the same. If it can only pass by reading the words, it should also read a fourth photograph it has never seen.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (last layer 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — a vote split across adjacent tiles still counts as knowing where you are; belief scattered across distant tiles still reads as unsure and the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: every training view is re-photographed at random before the model sees it — brightness, contrast, gamma, colour balance, saturation, blur and sensor grain all jittered independently per view — so the exact pixel values of one survey no longer predict the tile and only the shared street-and-building layout does. Tile labels, loss, paired three-survey batches, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py is untouched: CellLocNet, training_outputs(), forward(), loss_fn(), export_onnx() and the ONNX contract (train.py exports <out>/models/<area>.onnx taking a 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] and returning [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1], whole decode inside the graph) stay exactly as they are. The CLI contract stays exactly as it is: `python -m model.train --area A --out-dir D [--data-dir] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`, writing train_info.json as a list of per-area dicts.

1. Add module constants near BATCH_SIZE:
   AUG = dict(blur_p=0.7, blur_sigma_max=1.5, blur_taps=7, exposure=(0.75, 1.30), channel_gain=(0.85, 1.15), contrast=(0.6, 1.4), brightness=(-0.12, 0.12), gamma=(0.7, 1.4), saturation=(0.5, 1.5), noise_sigma_max=0.03)

2. Add a function `augment_views(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor` taking the float batch [B,3,H,W] in [0,1] on its device and returning a new tensor of the same shape, every random parameter drawn independently PER VIEW with torch.rand/torch.randn on x.device (the global torch seed is already set in train_area). Apply in this order:
   a. Blur (separable Gaussian, per-sample sigma): sigma = U(0, blur_sigma_max) per sample; with probability 1-blur_p set sigma to 0. Build a per-sample 1-D kernel over taps t in [-3..3]: k = exp(-t^2 / (2*max(sigma,0.05)^2)), normalised to sum 1 (sigma≈0 gives a delta, i.e. identity). Reshape x to [1, B*3, H, W], F.pad with mode='reflect' by 3 on the blurred axis, run F.conv2d with weight [B*3, 1, 7, 1] (kernel repeated across the 3 channels of each sample) and groups=B*3, then the same with [B*3, 1, 1, 7]; reshape back to [B,3,H,W]. Blur is applied first so that noise added later is NOT blurred.
   b. Gain: x = x * (exposure[B,1,1,1] * channel_gain[B,3,1,1]), each U() over its range.
   c. Contrast: m = x.mean(dim=(1,2,3), keepdim=True); x = m + c[B,1,1,1] * (x - m).
   d. Brightness: x = x + b[B,1,1,1].
   e. Gamma: x = x.clamp(1e-4, 1) ** g[B,1,1,1].
   f. Saturation: grey = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True); x = grey + s[B,1,1,1] * (x - grey).
   g. Noise: x = x + torch.randn_like(x) * n[B,1,1,1], n = U(0, noise_sigma_max).
   h. return x.clamp(0, 1).
   Keep it fully vectorised (no Python loop over samples); it must run on MPS, CUDA and CPU. Do not use torchvision transforms (per-sample parameters are required).

3. In train_area's inner loop, change the batch formation from
   `xb = x_u8[idx].to(device).float() / 255.0`
   to
   `xb = augment_views(x_u8[idx].to(device).float() / 255.0)`
   under model.train(). Everything downstream (training_outputs, make_soft_targets, residual_offset_target, loss_fn, top1/per-capture logging, scheduler) is unchanged. Do NOT augment anything at export time; export_onnx(model.cpu(), ...) stays as is.

4. Logging: in the returned info dict set `"capture_sampling": "paired-position interleave, shared heading per position, per-view photometric+sharpness nuisance randomisation"` and add `"augmentation": AUG` (JSON-serialisable: tuples become lists). Add a one-line comment above the top1 bookkeeping noting top1 is now measured on augmented views and will read lower than experiment 2's 0.79 by design. Update the module docstring with one short paragraph on the nuisance randomisation and why (fingerprints of one survey's exposure/sharpness no longer predict the cell).

5. Sanity before handing back: a 2-second smoke check that augment_views(torch.rand(8,3,128,128)) returns shape [8,3,128,128] within [0,1] and that with all ranges collapsed to identity (exposure=(1,1) etc., blur_p=0, noise 0) the output equals the input to 1e-5. Do not run training.

Contracts to preserve: train.py CLI flags and train_info.json format; ONNX export path and I/O (frozen scorer depends on them); epochs/views per epoch unchanged (EPOCHS comes from the harness); exported model size unchanged (3,079,093 bytes, under the 4 MiB gate); no file other than model/train.py touched; nothing under model/ may read the eval capture (load_scene already reads only buckets(meta, 'train') — leave it).
